title: Are two walls built with different cement equally strong?
description: A sixty foot wall with three bags of cement and a forty foot wall with two bags are compared by length to bags in simplest form. Keeko's doubt is that the wall with more bags is stronger.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare the length of wall to bags of cement as a ratio, not the bags alone. Watch for students who say more bags means a stronger wall.

source: Nitin builds a 60 ft wall with 3 bags of cement and Hari bui
video_script.why: The child uses proportional ratios to compare two walls built with different lengths and different amounts of cement.
video_script.substitution: Write length to bags for each wall, reduce each ratio to the simplest form, and compare them.
video_script.anchor: two walls: Leeza's wall 60 ft long with 3 bags of cement and Jia's wall 40 ft long with 2 bags
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the wall with three bags is stronger than the wall with two bags. That wall is also longer, sixty feet against forty, and both walls use one bag for every twenty feet, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Both walls use one bag for every twenty feet, so they are equally strong.

final_answer.value: Yes, both walls use one bag for every 20 ft, so they are equally strong
final_answer.spoken: yes, both walls use one bag for every twenty feet, so they are equally strong

names.Leeza: builds the 60 ft wall with 3 bags of cement
names.Jia: builds the 40 ft wall with 2 bags of cement

hold_back: Answer: yes, both walls use one bag for every 20 ft, so they are equally strong
maths_rules: both are 20 : 1, so 60 : 3 :: 40 : 2; each 20 ft of wall gets one bag
Keeko's slip: 3 bags are more than 2 bags, but 60 ft is also longer than 40 ft; 60 ÷ 3 = 20 ft for each bag and 40 ÷ 2 = 20 ft for each bag
video_script.design: One idea: length to bags as a ratio tells the strength. Assumes the simplest form test. Wrong idea: more bags means a stronger wall. The two walls stay for the whole video. No pronoun is used for the two builders.
